title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood Stage are forecast through at least midweek due to a combination of northerly winds and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north through the basin. Rises to Moderate Flood Stage are forecast later in the week due to the additional heavy rainfall expected. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor to Moderate flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 2.7 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 8:30 AM EST Tuesday was 2.7 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.4 feet Sunday morning. title: Flood Warning
description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues. * WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona... Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 24. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 815 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet. - Flooding is expected along the Gila River. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flash Flood Warning
description: FFWMFL The National Weather Service in Miami has extended the * Flash Flood Warning for... Northern Broward County in southeastern Florida... * Until 1100 PM EST. * At 952 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3 and 5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms. SOURCE...Radar indicated. IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor drainage and low-lying areas. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Coral Springs, Tamarac, Margate, Lauderhill, Coconut Creek, North Lauderdale, Lauderdale Lakes, Parkland, Broadview-Pompano Park, Godfrey Road, Village Park, Palm Aire and Ramblewood East.

title: Dense Fog Advisory
description: * WHAT...Visibility one quarter mile or less in dense fog. * WHERE...Odessa, Grand Coulee, Coulee City, Harrington, Quincy, Ritzville, Creston, Ephrata, Wilbur, Moses Lake, and Othello. * WHEN...Until 9 AM PST Wednesday. * IMPACTS...Low visibility could make driving conditions hazardous. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Fog will expand this evening with conditions deteriorating this evening into the overnight hours. North to northeast winds will pick up between 8AM and 10AM Wednesday morning, and the wind is expected to help break up the fog with conditions improving at that time.

title: Flash Flood Warning
description: FFWMFL The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a * Flash Flood Warning for... Southern Broward County in southeastern Florida... * Until 1130 PM EST. * At 931 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 3 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms. SOURCE...Radar indicated. IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor drainage and low-lying areas. * Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Hollywood, Davie, Plantation, Sunrise, Lauderhill, Cooper City, Nova Southeastern University, Pine Island Ridge, Broadview Park, Melrose Park, St. George, Washington Park, Chambers Estates, Downtown Davie and Broward Estates.

title: Special Marine Warning
description: SMWKEY The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a * Special Marine Warning for... Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to Halfmoon Shoal out 60 nm... * Until 1030 PM EST. * At 929 PM EST, a strong thunderstorm was located 15 nm south of Wood's Wall West Crack, moving northwest at 20 knots. HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater and small hail. SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist. IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours. * The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood Stage are forecast through at least midweek due to a combination of northerly winds and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north through the basin. Rises to Moderate Flood Stage are forecast later in the week due to the additional heavy rainfall expected. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 2.7 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 PM EST Tuesday was 2.7 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.4 feet Sunday morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County. .Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to continue to remain steady with slight deviations in river levels through mid to late week due to additional forecast heavy rainfall. For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage Fish Camp. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:15 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 17.1 feet. - Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:15 PM EST Tuesday was 17.1 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood stage at 17.1 feet. - Flood stage is 16.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas... Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring. * WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden. * WHEN...Until Wednesday afternoon. * IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding occurs, and causes sloughs and peripheral channels near the main stream to cut off areas of the flood plain, isolating livestock and damaging equipment in low areas. Oil field tank batteries and pump jacks flood. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 6:30 PM CST Tuesday the stage was 14.3 feet. - Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late this evening and continue falling to 11.2 feet by Sunday evening. - Flood stage is 14.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

title: Flood Warning
description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected. * WHERE...Munds Canyon and Oak Creek near Sedona. * WHEN...Until 1115 PM MST. * IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks and normally dry washes is occurring. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 532 PM MST, river gauges at Munds Canyon and Oak Creek near Sedona have both crested. However, water levels will remain elevated over the next few hours as water gradually decreases. - This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers... Oak Creek and Dry Beaver Creek. - For Oak Creek at Sedona: At 4:45pm the stage was 8.23 feet. Flood Stage is 14.0 feet. Forecast: A crest of 8.43 feet is expected by 7:00pm Tuesday. Impacts: At 5.0 feet: Multiple private low water crossings and bridges over Oak Creek above Sedona become impassable. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Sedona, Munds Park, Indian Gardens, Uptown Sedona, Red Rock State Park and Cathedral Rock. - This includes the following swimming holes... Midgely Bridge, Buddha Beach "Red Rock Crossing" and Crescent Moon Ranch. - Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

title: Flash Flood Warning
description: At 520 PM MST, a rise of 6 feet has occurred upstream of Page Springs at Sedona. The guage at Cornville has begun to rise, with a further rise expected in the next few hours. Flash flooding is already occurring. Flash flooding is expected to begin along Oak Creek in the Page Springs area within the next few hours. HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. SOURCE...River gauge reported. IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Oak Creek. Some locations that will experience flash flooding include... Cornville, Jordan, Page Springs and Bignotti. For Oak Creek at Cornville: At 5:00pm the stage was 2.01 feet. Flood Stage is 8.0 feet. Forecast: A crest of 9.17 feet is expected at 9:00pm Tuesday. Impacts: At 7.0 feet: Flooding begins to inundate lower terrace of RV park upstream of Page Springs Road Bridge. At 8.0 feet: Flooding of lower terrace of RV park upstream of Page Springs Road Bridge. At 9.0 feet: Hiking trails along banks of creek affected. Portions of residential yards flooded. This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds... Windmill Park. This includes the following swimming holes... Mormons Crossing. This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers... Oak Creek.
